newsitem.title: USA: Motorola cuts semiconductor officer pay.
newsitem.headline: Motorola cuts semiconductor officer pay.

text.p: Technology giant Motorola Inc's semiconductor group said on Monday it had cut the salaries of its elected officers by 10 percent as part of its recent efforts to reduce spending.
"These are elected officers of the semiconductor product sector worldwide," said Dan Rogers, director of public affairs for the company's semiconductor group in Austin, Tex., in an interview.
Rogers said the officers, who number about 30, are elected by the Motorola board of directors. The pay cuts were implemented in July, he said.

Cost-cutting measures were taken after the company reported lower second and third quarter earnings and sales versus last year, after having consistently reported revenue growth since 1985, Motorola said. The company said its semiconductor sector essentially broke even in the third quarter.

Motorola said it has reduced spending by halting construction plans, reducing work schedules, freezing hiring and offering voluntary severance packages. Earlier Monday, Rogers said the company cut 170 jobs at its Austin facility.
